title: [CQ-F09] Proxy attempt identity transport
description:
Objective: Transport current execution identities through the proxy without accepting caller identity substitution.

Deliverable: Proxy attempt identity transport. This is task F09 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F06.
definitionOfDone: Current attempt/session metadata survives MCP transport.
Legacy proxy and alternate CLI naming/framing regressions pass.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD the pure identity fence in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts. Write the tests first in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.test.ts: RED on the missing export, then GREEN. Iterate with focused runs (`npx vitest run src/utils.test.ts`) inside the scratch snapshot described in step 3, never in the shared tree.

Add, after injectRunnerIdentity:
- `export interface ExecutionIdentityRefusal { code: number; codeName: string; message: string }`
- `export function stampExecutionIdentity(parsed: unknown, env: Record<string, string | undefined>): boolean | ExecutionIdentityRefusal` (index.ts passes process.env).

The JSDoc gives the why: CQ-F09. The runner (the wrapper's env), never the CLI caller, owns the session's execution identity. It is the same transport idea as injectRunnerIdentity, except that the caller can never override the value.

Contract:
1. Tool table. Use a Map, never a plain-object index, so a tool named `constructor` or `toString` cannot hit a prototype-chain key. Key it by every spelling (`moe.x`, `moe_x`, `x`), as CLAIM_TOOL does.
   - get_context carries [sessionId].
   - start_step carries [attemptId, generation, sessionId]: CQ-F07's optional inputs.
   - Nothing else is touched. That includes claim_next_task, heartbeat, reattach_attempt and release_task, which carry attempt fields of their own; complete_step/complete_task, whose contract CQ-F08 owns; every other tool; tools/list; and non-tools/call methods.
2. Shape guards, as injectRunnerIdentity: a tools/call, object params, a string name in the table, and `arguments` a non-null, non-array object. Anything else returns false and is left untouched.
3. Env groups. Blank means undefined, '' or whitespace-only: the MOE_WORKER_ID rule (grok expands `${VAR:-}` to '').
   - Session group, MOE_SESSION_ID. Blank means absent. Otherwise it is valid only under the daemon's sessionId rule (readContextSessionId in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts): at most 255 UTF-16 units, no NUL, no CR, no LF. It is sent verbatim, never trimmed.
   - Attempt group, MOE_ATTEMPT_ID + MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, both or neither. Both blank means absent; exactly one blank means partial.
   - attemptId must fully match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/: the wrapper's pin_attempt_identity rule and start_step's 128-char bound.
   - generation must fully match /^[1-9][0-9]*$/ and pass Number.isSafeInteger, and is sent as a JSON number. A sign, exponent, decimal point, leading zero or surrounding whitespace is malformed. Never trim or parseInt.
4. Decision. Consider only the groups the tool carries, so a broken attempt group never blocks get_context.
   a. A carried group that is malformed or partial returns { code: -32602, codeName: 'EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID', message }. The message names the tool, the env variable(s) and the broken rule.
   b. Otherwise, check each field of each present group. If the field is an own property (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call) whose value is not === the env value, return { code: -32003, codeName: 'EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED', message }. The message names the tool, the field and its env variable, and tells the caller to omit the field so the proxy supplies the session's own value. A string '7' against generation 7, a null, or another attempt's id is refused, never coerced.
   c. Otherwise, set every missing field from env and return true. Return true also when every field was already present and equal, so index.ts forwards the exact object it checked, never the raw line.
   d. If no carried group is present, return false: this is the legacy proxy. Caller-presented identity fields, even partial or malformed ones, pass through untouched, and the daemon decides (assertAttemptCurrent, readContextSessionId, CQ-F07's strict gate).
   - Decide everything before mutating, so a refusal leaves `arguments` untouched.
   - Messages never echo an env or argument value.
5. Error handling: like its siblings it never throws, but it fails closed. An unexpected exception returns an EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID refusal, never an unstamped forward.

Tests: one new describe('stampExecutionIdentity'), table-driven. Assert whole-object toEqual on `arguments`, and both code and codeName on refusals.
- Legacy: env {} and an all-blank env ('' and '  ') return false and leave args unchanged for get_context and start_step. That includes caller-presented partial or malformed identity ({attemptId:'x'}, {generation:'7'}).
- A session-only env gives get_context and start_step only sessionId.
- A full env makes start_step's arguments exactly {taskId, stepId, attemptId, generation: 7 (typeof number), sessionId}. get_context gains only sessionId: no attemptId or generation key.
- Presented-equal values (all three, and each alone) return true, and the arguments end up complete.
- Substitution, one field at a time (another attempt id, generation '7', 8, null, sessionId plus a trailing space): EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED -32003, with args equal to a pre-call copy.
- Partial env (id only; generation only): start_step gets EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID -32602 with args unchanged, while get_context under the same env still gets sessionId.
- Malformed env table, each case EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID with no field added. A distinctive marker value never appears in the message.
  - generation: '0', '07', '+7', '7.0', '1e3', ' 7', '7 ', '7' plus a LF, '-1', 'abc', '9007199254740992'.
  - attemptId: 'a b', 'a/b', 'é', 129 chars.
  - sessionId: 256 chars; one containing a LF, a CR or a NUL.
  - Boundaries accepted: generation '9007199254740991', a 128-char attemptId, a 255-char sessionId.
- Names: moe_start_step, start_step, and a moe_ alias resolved by resolveToolCallName all stamp. With a full env, these all return false without throwing: claim_next_task, complete_step, complete_task, heartbeat, get_activity_log, tools/list, `constructor`, `toString`, and odd shapes (null, params null, a numeric name, arguments null/array/missing).

Budget: about 210 added lines or fewer (function about 80, tests about 130).

stampExecutionIdentity + ExecutionIdentityRefusal added to utils.ts (+104), with 10 new tests in utils.test.ts (+131).
- The tool table is a Map keyed by all three spellings: get_context carries the session group, start_step carries the attempt and session groups.
- Env groups: MOE_SESSION_ID, and MOE_ATTEMPT_ID + MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION (both or neither). Blank means absent.
- Refusal codes: -32602 EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID and -32003 EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED. Everything is decided before any mutation, and an unexpected exception fails closed.
RED: 10 failed (missing export). GREEN: utils.test.ts 67/67, `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Both ran in the Linux scratch snapshot /tmp/moe-f09-gate.7BYVde (native npm ci; lockfile sha equals HEAD's, ignoring CR).
Mutation probes: 7/7 killed (loose !=, no isSafeInteger, {1,129}, no NUL check, a read short-circuit, catch returning false, partial check removed).
The 520 dirty paths from other sessions were left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Wire the fence into the transport in packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts, with end-to-end tests in packages/moe-proxy/src/index.test.ts, and make the suite hermetic in packages/moe-proxy/vitest.config.ts.

index.ts: in the stdin line handler, the fence runs after resolveToolCallName, injectWorkerId and injectRunnerIdentity, and before the tools/list bookkeeping, pending tracking and queueing.
- Single message: `const identity = stampExecutionIdentity(parsed, process.env)`. On a refusal:
  - Write ONE id-aware JSON-RPC error. The id is the request's string or number id, else null.
  - Set error.data to { tool: params.name, codeName }, mirroring the daemon's errors. Give writeErrorWithId an optional `data` argument; existing callers stay unchanged.
  - Log `Refused <tool>: <codeName>` to stderr, without values, then `continue`.
  - A refused request is never forwarded, never queued while disconnected, and never added to pendingRequestIds/pendingRequestTimes, so no later timeout or shutdown error can duplicate its id.
- JSON-RPC batch. The daemon executes arrays of up to 25 requests (McpAdapter.handle), and today the proxy forwards arrays untouched. A batch must not bypass the fence, so apply stampExecutionIdentity to each element.
  - If any element is refused, forward nothing. Write ONE JSON array holding an error for every element whose id is a string or number. Each error carries the first refusal's code and data, with the message prefixed `batch refused: `.
  - When no element has such an id, write a single error with id null.
  - Batches otherwise keep today's behaviour: no per-element alias mapping or workerId injection (out of scope).
- Payload: re-serialize when renamed || mutated || stamped || the identity result is true (an identity-stamped batch element counts). Otherwise forward the raw line byte-for-byte: the legacy path.

vitest.config.ts: add test.env setting each of these to '': MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_SESSION_ID, MOE_ATTEMPT_ID, MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION, MOE_RUNNER_PROCESS_STARTED_AT, MOE_RUNNER_HOST, MOE_DAEMON_HOST, MOE_TOOL_NAME_STYLE, MOE_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS.
- Every reader treats blank as unset, and vitest 5 assigns test.env to process.env before tests run.
- Why: agent seats export MOE_SESSION_ID, plus MOE_DAEMON_HOST in WSL agent mode, and every spawn here inherits {...process.env}. Without the blanking, the existing runner-identity test's exact get_context arguments fail in any seat once sessionId is stamped.
- One choke point instead of per-test env scrubbing. A test that needs a value sets it explicitly.

index.test.ts: inside the existing describe (reuse its beforeEach mock daemon), add one small local spawn helper that records the raw frames the daemon receives and the stdout lines. Add three tests, RED before the wiring:
1. 'carries the session execution identity to start_step and get_context under the underscore alias style'.
   - Env: MOE_WORKER_ID 'worker-t', MOE_SESSION_ID 'worker-t@2026-10-26T00:00:00Z', MOE_ATTEMPT_ID 'attempt-0123', MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION '3', MOE_TOOL_NAME_STYLE 'underscore'.
   - Calls: moe_start_step {taskId:'task-1', stepId:'step-1'}, moe_get_context {taskId:'task-1'}, moe.claim_next_task {statuses:['WORKING']}.
   - The daemon sees exactly: moe.start_step {taskId, stepId, workerId, attemptId:'attempt-0123', generation:3, sessionId}; moe.get_context {taskId, workerId, sessionId}; and a claim with workerId only.
   - The mock daemon answers get_context with text carrying servedContext {attemptId, generation, receiptId, packetId}. That stdout line equals the daemon's frame byte-for-byte, which proves the response metadata survives.
2. 'refuses caller substitution without forwarding, keeping stdin framing'.
   - Same env. ONE stdin write carries: start_step id 10 with attemptId 'attempt-other'; ping id 11; a batch [start_step id 12 with generation '3']; start_step id 13 presenting the equal identity.
   - Expect an error for id 10 with code -32003 and data.codeName EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED, an array response erroring id 12, and answers for 11 and 13.
   - The daemon receives only ids [11, 13].
   - Then end stdin. The proxy exits with no second response for id 10.
3. 'is the legacy proxy when the session carries no identity'.
   - The identity env and MOE_WORKER_ID are blank.
   - A start_step line with irregular inner spacing (none leading or trailing: the proxy trims frames) presenting {attemptId:'x'} reaches the daemon as the identical raw string, and its reply is forwarded unchanged.

Budget: about 140 added lines or fewer (index.ts about 30, config about 12, tests about 100).

- fenceExecutionIdentity runs last in the stdin line handler, after the rename/workerId/runner stamps and before the tools/list bookkeeping, tracking and queueing.
- A batch is checked element by element. Any refusal drops the whole frame untracked, and writeIdentityRefusal writes ONE id-aware error, or ONE array of errors prefixed `batch refused: `, with data {tool, codeName}. stderr gets `Refused <tool>: <codeName>`, with no values.

Run the gate once, fresh: `cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test`. pretest builds with tsc, so this run is also the typecheck. Supply its command, exit code 0 and output tail to moe.complete_task.

The gate covers the new tests and the legacy regressions:
- utils.test.ts.
- The existing index.test.ts: alias naming, timeouts, shutdown, oversized lines, runner identity.
- input-framing.test.ts.

Never run the gate in the shared checkout:
- packages/moe-proxy/node_modules there is a Windows install (@esbuild/win32-x64 and the win32 TypeScript binary).
- `npm test` first runs `npm run clean`, which deletes the shared packages/moe-proxy/dist that IDE plugin builds bundle, and then tries a build that cannot succeed from WSL.

Recipe (Linux/WSL):
1. `SNAP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-f09-gate.XXXXXX)`, then `git archive HEAD packages/moe-proxy | tar -x -C "$SNAP"`.
2. Copy the five task files over and `cmp` each one against the worktree.

Expect zero failing tests. A failure is a defect to fix with systematic-debugging, never one to skip; that is this gate's error handling. Record the pass counts and the snapshot path in the step note. Afterwards rm -rf the snapshot, checking the path prefix first.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review: load adversarial-self-review and review the whole task diff, `git diff -- packages/moe-proxy`. Check each point:
- Bypass. Can a caller reach the daemon with an identity other than the env's? Try a batch, a duplicate JSON key (the checked object is what gets forwarded, not the raw line), an alias spelling, a prototype-chain tool name, and arguments that are null, an array or missing.
- Coercion. Is any env or argument value trimmed, loosely parsed or type-converted? Is a refusal ever followed by a partial mutation or a forward?
- Framing. Is a refused id ever tracked, queued, timed out or answered twice? Does a refusal inside a multi-line stdin chunk leave the following lines intact?
- Legacy. With no identity env, is every frame byte-identical to before? With a full env, are tools outside the table untouched?
- Error handling. Is every error id-aware, with no value echoed and nothing sensitive written to stderr?
- Seat env. Does the suite stay green with MOE_SESSION_ID and MOE_DAEMON_HOST exported?
- Scope. Did only the five planned files change (no .moe edits, no git writes)? Are there no forbidden-pattern tokens? Is the net LOC 400 or less including tests (`git diff --numstat`)?

Fix any finding with a focused test. If anything changed, re-run the step 3 gate fresh and supply that output to moe.complete_task.

The completion summary states:

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of `git diff -- packages/moe-proxy`. No defects found and no code changed, so the step-3 gate output stands: all five files were cmp-identical to the gated snapshot before it was removed.
- Bypass. The daemon (McpAdapter) looks tools up in an exact `moe.<name>` Map. Handlers receive only params.arguments. Batches run element by element, and a nested array returns null. So a batch, an alias, or a prototype-name trick cannot get past the fence. Batch elements are fenced against every spelling. Duplicate JSON keys: the checked object is the one forwarded when stamped, and both sides use JSON.parse (last key wins). A JSON-defined prototype-named own key in arguments cannot shadow the stamped own property. Arguments that are missing, null or an array return false; the daemon then refuses on taskId, and verified-local refuses STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED.
- Coercion. The env values are verbatim, and generation is checked with strict regex + isSafeInteger before Number(). Arguments are compared with ===. A refusal decides before any mutation; a batch mutated before a refusal is dropped whole.
- Framing. A refusal `continue`s before tracking or queueing, so there is no timeout or shutdown duplicate. Test 2 proves the following lines in the same chunk survive and that the daemon saw only [11, 13].
- Legacy. With no env, every element returns false and the raw line goes out byte-for-byte (test 3). The batch path is unchanged when nothing is stamped.
- Errors. Every refusal is id-aware with data {tool, codeName}. Messages name only the tool, field and env var; tests assert no value or marker is echoed. stderr gets codeName only.
- Seat env. Hostile exports gave 84/84 (MOE_SESSION_ID, an unreachable MOE_DAEMON_HOST, MOE_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS=1, a full attempt identity, underscore style).
- Scope. Only the 5 planned files changed: +373/-3, net 370 of the 400 allowed. No forbidden tokens, no .moe edits, no git writes.
Not a defect, noted for QA: a JSON number 3.0 equals generation 3 (indistinguishable after parse), and a notification refusal answers with id null, as planned.

comments.content:
Interface note from CQ-F07 (task-3918d119, plan rev 1, TURBO-approved; re-check against F07's landed code before you build on it). moe.start_step gains three OPTIONAL inputs:
- attemptId: string, at most 128 chars.
- generation: integer, at least 1.
- sessionId: string with get_context's rules (non-blank, at most 255 chars, no NUL or line breaks).

How the daemon treats them:
- In every profile, a malformed value is refused INVALID_INPUT and never coerced.
- In every profile, a presented attemptId/generation goes through assertAttemptCurrent, so a superseded, closed or future attempt gets ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED before any write.
- Under verified-local, workerId, attemptId, generation and sessionId are all required (STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED). The attempt's served-context receipt must name that same sessionId, so a step-entry call has to carry the same session incarnation the get_context read carried (the wrapper's MOE_SESSION_ID).

For this transport task: carry attemptId, generation and sessionId to moe.start_step and moe.get_context unchanged. Never let the CLI caller substitute them, and never inject a malformed value: the daemon refuses it in legacy too. F07 changes no proxy code.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Caller-wins injection like MOE_WORKER_ID: rejected, because it accepts caller substitution.
2. Inject the raw env strings and let the daemon validate: rejected. generation needs a typed conversion, which risks coercion, and CQ-F07 says never inject a malformed value.
3. Learn the identity from claim/get_context responses passing through the proxy: rejected. The wrapper's pre-flight claim never crosses the CLI's proxy, and response-derived state would be a second identity authority (epic rail).
4. Bind the attempt env to a task id: rejected. Workers never claim in-session (docs/roles/worker.md), so the session's one attempt is the only one start_step may carry, and a stale identity on another task fails closed at the daemon (ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED).
5. Exit the proxy at startup on a malformed env: rejected, because it would kill every moe.* tool. Only the calls that would carry the broken group are refused.
6. Cover complete_step/complete_task now: rejected. CQ-F08 (BACKLOG) owns their contract; a hand-forward note is posted.
7. Scrub MOE_* per test instead of in vitest test.env: rejected. One choke point fixes every spawn, including the existing runner-identity test.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- McpAdapter never validates arguments against inputSchema. additionalProperties:false is only advisory, and handlers read only their own fields, so a pre-F07 start_step simply ignores the stamped fields.
- The daemon executes JSON-RPC batches of up to 25 (McpAdapter.handle), while the proxy forwards arrays untouched. The fence must therefore cover batch elements.
- Precedent: injectRunnerIdentity (commit a4430849). Env goes onto claim args; both or neither; blank means unset; values are verbatim; three name spellings.
- The wrappers already export MOE_SESSION_ID before the pre-flight claim (moe-agent.sh ~6119, moe-agent.ps1 ~5571). MOE_ATTEMPT_ID/MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION are unexported shell variables set by pin_attempt_identity (moe-agent.sh ~2139-2156). CQ-F10/F11 export them and add them to codex's seat_keys and grok's env lines.
- Daemon rules mirrored:
  - sessionId: readContextSessionId (non-blank, at most 255, no NUL/CR/LF, verbatim).
  - attemptId: at most 128 (start_step), matching the wrapper's [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}.
  - generation: a positive safe integer.
- Live seats run the installed plugin's proxy, not packages/moe-proxy/dist, so this change reaches the fleet only through a plugin rebuild.
planningNotes.risks:
- Seat env leaks. Agent seats export MOE_SESSION_ID, plus MOE_DAEMON_HOST in WSL agent mode, and spawned proxies inherit {...process.env}. The test.env blanking fixes the suite; the gate still runs with MOE_* unset.
- The shared checkout's packages/moe-proxy/node_modules is a Windows install, and `npm test` there runs clean first, deleting the shared dist. Run the gate only in a scratch snapshot.
- Once a seat runs this proxy, the wrapper's own one-shot get_context calls (pre-flight, post-flight, adoption) carry MOE_SESSION_ID and mint receipts.
  - Pre-flight is intended. Post-flight and adoption should move to view:"status" (CQ-F10/F11).
  - Harmless meanwhile: a receipt is never approval, and verified-local stays unavailable.
- codex, grok and gemini seats see none of these variables until CQ-F10/F11 add them to their MCP env tables. The proxy stays legacy for them, by design.
- A caller-supplied workerId still wins (unchanged legacy). The daemon binds receipts and attempts to the owning worker, so a foreign workerId gains nothing from the stamped identity.
- QA cap: 400 net LOC or less including tests; target about 350.
- Rail grep: never spell the project's forbidden-pattern tokens in code or tests. Prototype-name tests use `constructor`/`toString`.

completionSummary:
CQ-F09 delivered (plan rev 1, 4/4 steps). The proxy carries the session's execution identity, and a caller can never substitute its own. 5 files, +373/-3 (net 370).
Env contract (CQ-F10/F11 build on it). A blank value counts as absent.
- MOE_SESSION_ID: at most 255 chars, no NUL/CR/LF, sent verbatim.
- MOE_ATTEMPT_ID + MOE_ATTEMPT_GENERATION: both or neither. attemptId must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}. generation must match ^[1-9][0-9]*$ and be a safe integer, and is sent as a JSON number. Values are never trimmed or loosely parsed.
Stamping covers ONLY get_context (sessionId) and start_step (attemptId, generation, sessionId), under every spelling (moe.x, moe_x, x). A Map is used, so names like constructor/toString do nothing.
codeNames (error.data {tool, codeName}):
- EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED -32003: a presented field !== the env value. '7' vs 7, null, another attempt id, or a trailing space are all refused, never coerced.
- EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID -32602: a carried env group is malformed or partial, or an unexpected error occurred (fails closed). A broken attempt group never blocks get_context.
With no carried group it is the legacy proxy: the raw line is forwarded byte-for-byte and the daemon decides.
index.ts:
- The fence runs last in the stdin handler, so it checks exactly what gets forwarded.
- JSON-RPC batches are fenced per element, so a batch cannot bypass it. Any refusal drops the whole frame, untracked and never queued: ONE id-aware error, or an array of errors prefixed `batch refused: `.
- No value is echoed, and stderr gets the codeName only.

Reviewed completion commit 4ea8783 (on moe/work-2026-10-24, pushed). Code is +373/-3 (net 370, at most 400) across utils.ts/index.ts/vitest.config.ts plus 2 test files; no forbidden tokens.

Gate re-run fresh: `cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test` exit 0, 84/84 (utils 67, input-framing 3, index 14), and the pretest tsc build passed. It ran in a Linux snapshot (git archive 4ea8783 packages/moe-proxy, 5 files cmp-identical to the commit, native npm ci, env -i). It also passes with hostile seat env exported (MOE_SESSION_ID, MOE_DAEMON_HOST unreachable, full attempt identity, MOE_MESSAGE_TIMEOUT_MS=1, underscore style), 84/84.

DoD:
1. Identity survives transport. e2e test 1 shows the daemon receives start_step {attemptId, generation:3 (a number), sessionId} and get_context {sessionId} under alias style, and the servedContext reply comes back byte-identical.
2. Malformed or partial env gives EXECUTION_IDENTITY_INVALID -32602; substitution gives EXECUTION_IDENTITY_SUBSTITUTED -32003, with strict === and no mutation or echo. Batches are fenced per element and refused frames are never tracked or queued.
3. Legacy raw-byte passthrough (test 3), the alias, framing, timeout, shutdown and runner-identity suites all pass.
4. Evidence was supplied.

Daemon parity: proxy rules match readContextSessionId/validateStringValue (at most 255, no NUL/CR/LF, non-blank, verbatim). get_context from a non-owner returns unrecorded rather than refusing. Legacy start_step only validates sessionId, so live QA/architect seats aren't broken.

My mutation probes were all killed: batch left unfenced, refused frame forwarded, loose !=.

Non-blocking notes:
- A refused notification gets an id:null error (as planned; JSON-RPC says notifications get no reply).
- Under a session-only env, a caller-presented attemptId passes to the daemon (assertAttemptCurrent), as planned.
- The landing commit also staged peer board record .moe/tasks/task-c619879…json (wrapper board-state staging, not this task's code).
